DISCOVERY 612, DEFENDANTS' MOTION TO COMPEL DEPOSITIONS AND OTHER DISCOVERY NOTICED PRIOR TO THE DISCOVERY CUT-OFF IS GRANTED IN PART AND DENIED IN PART. THE MOTION IS DENIED AS IT SEEKS TO COMPEL THE DEPOSITION OF THE PERSON MOST KNOWLEDGEABLE. THE OMISSION OF ANY REFERENCE TO THE MATTERS ON WHICH EXAMINATION WAS SOUGHT WAS THE BASIS OF A PROPER OBJECTION. THE NOTICE OF DEPOSITION WAS PURSUANT TO C.C.P. SECTION 2025.220 AND NOT C.C.P. SECTION 2020.420. THE AMENDED NOTICE WAS UNTIMELY AND INVALID. THE MOTION IS DENIED AS TO SUYAMA. THE MOTION IS DENIED AS TO TIMOTHY RYAN AND TRITIA MURATA. THE OBJECTIONS WERE TIMELY, AND THE AMENDED NOTICES WERE NOT TIMELY. THE MOTION IS GRANTED AS TO B. SCOTT SILVERMAN ON A DATE AND TIME AGREED UPON BY THE WITNESS AND COUNSEL. THE FURTHER DEPOSITION IS LIMITED TO ONE DAY. THE MOTION IS DENIED AS TO THE DEPOSITION OF MICHAEL CHAMBERLIN AS HIS DEPOSITION WAS CONDITIONED UPON AN ORDER TO PRODUCE DOCUMENTS PURSUANT TO THE PERSON MOST KNOWLEDGEABLE DEPOSITION. THE MOTION IS DENIED AS TO MARCUS TORRANO WHO WAS SUBPOENAED FOR HIS DEPOSITION AS A FORMER EMPLOYEE. HE WAS NOT SERVED WITH NOTICE OF THIS MOTION. AS THE MOTION SEEKS AN AFTER THE FACT FINDING THAT THE NOTICES WERE PROPERLY SERVED ON SHORTENED TIME, THE MOTION IS DENIED. COMMISSIONER EVERETT A. HEWLETT, JR. MATTER NOT REPORTED.
